name: usecase-purchase-request
title: Purchase request use case (reserve + enqueue)
description: RequestPurchaseUseCase: validate, honor Idempotency-Key (return existing order), atomically reserve inventory with 10-minute expiry, persist order as RESERVED, publish to the order queue and return orderId immediately. If publishing fails after reserving, release the reservation and mark the order failed. NOTES (from F-009 review): (1) Idempotency: a GSI cannot enforce uniqueness and is eventually consistent, so derive the orderId deterministically from the Idempotency-Key (or write a key-reservation item with attribute_not_exists) so two concurrent requests with the same key cannot create two orders. (2) Stay within the five spec states: a failed/compensated order ends in AVAILABLE and the reason is recorded in the audit entry; do NOT add EXPIRED/FAILED states (the spec has exactly AVAILABLE, RESERVED, PENDING_CONFIRMATION, SOLD, COMPLIMENTARY). (3) Prefer OrderRepository.transition over saveAuditEntry so status and audit stay atomic. (4) Order and inventory writes are separate: design the compensation/ordering so a crash between them cannot oversell (reserve inventory first, then create the order; release on failure).
acceptance: Returns orderId without waiting for processing
Same Idempotency-Key never creates a second order or reserves twice
Reservation expiry is exactly now + 10 minutes (configurable, tested with a fixed Clock)
Publish failure compensates by releasing inventory

name: usecase-order-status
title: Order status query use case
description: GetOrderStatusUseCase returning current status (any of the five states), quantity, event and expiry; OrderNotFound otherwise.
acceptance: Returns the current status for existing orders
Unknown order id yields OrderNotFound
Unit tests cover each status value

name: usecase-process-order
title: Process order use case (consumer logic)
description: ProcessOrderUseCase: idempotent handling of an order message: RESERVED -> PENDING_CONFIRMATION -> SOLD, validating the reservation is still valid (not expired) and real inventory. Reprocessing a SOLD order is a no-op. Expired reservations end released. NOTE (from F-008 review): InventoryRepository has no operations for the pendingConfirmation counter yet (reserve, confirmSale, release, issueComplimentary only); extend the port and adapter (e.g. markPending: reserved -> pendingConfirmation, and confirm/release from pendingConfirmation) as part of this feature. NOTES (from F-009 review): treat OrderStatusConflictException and OrderNotFoundException from reprocessing as benign (idempotent redelivery; GSI reads are eventually consistent). Order transition and inventory update are two writes: order them so a crash cannot leave a sale without inventory movement (or document the reconciliation). NOTE (from F-012 review): reuse OrderPlacementRepository.releaseReservation for the expired-reservation path; releaseReservation accepts PENDING_CONFIRMATION.
acceptance: Processing the same message twice yields the same final state and counters
Expired reservation is not sold and its inventory is released
Transitions are audited
Concurrent processing of the same order results in a single sale

name: sqs-publisher
title: SQS order queue publisher adapter
description: Implement OrderQueuePublisher with the AWS SDK v2 async SQS client. Message body is a versioned JSON record with orderId; include message attributes for tracing. Retry with backoff on transient errors. NOTE (from F-012 review): UseCaseConfig currently wires an always-error OrderQueuePublisher fallback until the SQS adapter exists; remove that fallback and wire the real SQS publisher here.
acceptance: Publishing returns after SQS acknowledges the message
Integration test with LocalStack verifies the message arrives
Endpoint and queue URL come from configuration

name: sqs-consumer
title: SQS consumer with at-least-once semantics and DLQ
description: Reactive long-polling consumer that calls ProcessOrderUseCase and deletes the message only after success. Configure visibility timeout, maxReceiveCount and DLQ redrive. Bounded concurrency; graceful shutdown. NOTE (from F-012 review): if the process dies between the placement transaction and the publish, an order stays RESERVED with no queue message (reclaimed on expiry); also the consumer must ignore messages whose order is no longer RESERVED (e.g. released after a failed publish). NOTE (from F-014 review): ProcessOrderUseCase returns a sealed ProcessOrderResult (Sold, ReleasedAsExpired, AlreadyProcessed, OrderMissing): ack the message for all of them; let transient errors and a final OrderStatusConflictException (after 5 re-reads) propagate so SQS redelivers. If a worker dies between the two steps (RESERVED->PENDING_CONFIRMATION, ->SOLD) recovery relies on SQS redelivery (or the expiry sweep).
acceptance: Message is deleted only after successful processing
Failed processing makes the message reappear and, after maxReceiveCount, land in the DLQ (integration test)
Concurrency is bounded by configuration
Poison messages (invalid JSON) do not stop the consumer

name: reservation-expiration-job
title: Scheduled release of expired reservations
description: Reactive scheduler that periodically finds expired reservations and, per order, atomically transitions it to expired and returns inventory to available. Safe under multiple app instances (conditional transition ensures one winner). NOTES (from F-009 review): expired reservations end in AVAILABLE (no EXPIRED state; spec: tickets return to available inventory), with the reason in the audit entry. findExpiredReservations is GSI-based (eventually consistent): rely on OrderRepository.transition's conditional write so concurrent sweepers have a single winner and treat OrderStatusConflictException as benign. NOTE (from F-012 review): use OrderPlacementRepository.releaseReservation (single TransactWriteItems: conditional order update + audit + inventory reserved->available; accepts RESERVED and PENDING_CONFIRMATION) for expiry, instead of separate writes. An order whose publish never happened stays RESERVED and is reclaimed here. NOTE (from F-014 review): align the expiry boundary: ProcessOrderUseCase treats expiresAt <= now as expired while docs/architecture.md and OrderRepository.findExpiredReservations use expiresAt < now; make them consistent (update docs and the query or the use case) and test the boundary. Also reuse OrderPlacementRepository.releaseReservation (already used by ProcessOrderUseCase for the expired path).
acceptance: Expired reservations return their quantity to available exactly once
Non-expired reservations are untouched
Two concurrent runs never release the same order twice
Interval is configurable and tested with a virtual clock

name: web-events-api
title: Events REST endpoints
description: POST /events, GET /events/{id}, GET /events with request/response DTOs as records and bean validation.
acceptance: POST /events returns 201 with Location header
Invalid body returns 400 with a structured error

WebTestClient tests for each endpoint

name: web-orders-availability-api
title: Orders and availability REST endpoints
description: POST /orders (Idempotency-Key header, returns 202 + orderId), GET /orders/{id}, GET /events/{id}/availability and GET /events/{id}/availability/stream (text/event-stream). NOTE (from F-011 review): GetAvailabilityUseCase.stream ends with an error once DynamoDB transient-error retries are exhausted; the SSE endpoint must resubscribe/retry with backoff (e.g. Flux.retryWhen) and never leak internal error details to the client. NOTE (from F-012 review): map IdempotentOrderNotActiveException (replayed key whose order was released) and IdempotencyKeyReusedException to non-202 responses (409); OrderEnqueueFailedException to a 5xx/503 telling the client to retry with a new Idempotency-Key. NOTE (from F-013 review): OrderStatusView exposes reservationExpiresAt even for SOLD/COMPLIMENTARY orders; omit it from the REST response DTO when the status is final.
acceptance: POST /orders returns 202 immediately with orderId
Missing or malformed Idempotency-Key returns 400
Availability stream produces server-sent events
WebTestClient tests for each endpoint

name: web-error-handling
title: Global reactive error handling
description: Central handler mapping domain exceptions to RFC 7807 problem details: 404, 409 (insufficient inventory, concurrent modification), 410 (expired reservation), 400, 429 and 500 without leaking internals.
acceptance: Each domain exception maps to the documented status
500 responses never expose stack traces or internal messages
A correlation id is included in error responses and logs

name: complimentary-issuance
title: Issue complimentary tickets
description: Use case and endpoint POST /events/{id}/complimentary that moves tickets AVAILABLE -> COMPLIMENTARY. Final state, excluded from sales totals.
acceptance: Cannot exceed available inventory
Complimentary tickets are not counted as sold in any report or counter
Transition is audited

name: concurrency-tests
title: End-to-end concurrency and consistency tests
description: Integration tests that fire many parallel purchase requests over limited capacity and assert no oversell, correct counters, no duplicate orders for the same Idempotency-Key and correct release after expiry. NOTE (from F-014 review): audit sort keys are <timestamp>#<uuid>, so two entries in the same instant order randomly and clock skew between nodes could reorder them; the integration tests use a clock advancing 1 ms per read. Consider asserting audit ORDER only where the timestamps are strictly increasing, and document the limitation. NOTE (from F-019 review): add an end-to-end test for POST /orders with a non-existent eventId (the 404 mapping exists but is untested end to end).
acceptance: N parallel requests over capacity C never produce sold + reserved > C
Counter invariant holds at the end of every scenario
Duplicate message delivery does not double-sell
Tests are deterministic (no flaky sleeps)

name: security-hardening
title: Security hardening
description: Secrets only via env vars, request size limits, per-client rate limiting on POST /orders, max quantity per order, input validation, idempotency protection against malicious retries, dependency vulnerability scan in CI, and non-root, minimal runtime image. NOTE (from F-012 review): scope the Idempotency-Key per principal/client so one client cannot collide with or probe another's orders (OrderId is derived from the key alone); do not cancel the purchase pipeline on client disconnect (e.g. detach the reserve/publish chain from the request subscription). NOTE (from F-017 review): SqsOrderConsumer and ReservationExpirationScheduler share a `running` flag across runs; a stop() followed by start() while a previous drain/sweep is still running can overlap the old loop with the new one (data-safe thanks to conditional writes, but wasteful). Fix both lifecycles with a per-start generation token captured in the repeat predicate, and add a restart-during-drain test. NOTE (from F-019 review): if a client disconnects after the reservation transaction and before the message is published, the order stays RESERVED with no queue message and a replay of the same Idempotency-Key returns 202 WITHOUT republishing until the reservation expires (the expiry scheduler is off by default outside docker-compose). Fix: on a replay whose existing order is still RESERVED, republish the message (duplicates are safe: the consumer is idempotent) and/or detach the reserve+publish chain from the request subscription so a disconnect cannot cancel it; add a test that simulates the disconnect. NOTES (from F-020 review): (1) 404 details echo the path id (e.g. 'Event not found: ../../etc'): validate id format at the web layer (or stop echoing unvalidated input) so user input is never reflected; (2) a DynamoDB/SQS outage currently surfaces as a generic 500: map transient infrastructure failures (throttling, timeouts, connection errors) to 503 + Retry-After via the existing ApiExceptionHandler; (3) Netty-level rejections (malformed URL like /%zz, illegal header characters) return an empty 400 without X-Correlation-Id: acceptable, but document it; (4) throw the web-level RateLimitExceededException (already mapped to 429 + Retry-After by F-020) from the rate limiter. NOTES (from F-021 review): rate-limit failed X-Admin-Key attempts (brute-force protection) on the admin routes in addition to POST /orders; the audit actor of complimentary issuance is a fixed string ('complimentary-issuance'): document that it should carry the caller identity once real authentication exists; 401 (wrong key) vs 403 (no key configured) reveals that the server has no key set: acceptable for a local/dev setup, document it in docs/security.md. PROGRESS: PART 1 (application-level hardening) is merged via PR 'F-023a': rate limiting (per client, bounded, XFF only if trusted), failed admin-key lockout, 413 body limit, Idempotency-Key min length 16, validated path ids, republish on replay of a RESERVED order, detached purchase chain, lifecycle generation tokens, 503 for transient infrastructure errors, security headers, secret masking. REMAINING = PART 2 (supply chain and infrastructure): dependency vulnerability scan + secret scanning in CI (pinned action SHAs), Dependabot (gradle, github-actions, docker), container/compose hardening (resource limits, read_only, cap_drop, no-new-privileges, minimal JRE image, HEALTHCHECK), and docs/security.md with the threat model including these LIMITATIONS flagged by the part 1 review: IPv6 clients are keyed per full address (a /64 gives effectively unlimited identities: bucket by /64 or rely on an edge layer, see F-026), the limiter is per instance, the admin lockout is per client address so a shared address can lock the real admin out for ~20 s per token, Idempotency-Key is not scoped per principal (there is no user authentication: mitigated by the 16-char minimum and by deriving the OrderId with SHA-256 so the key cannot be recovered from an order id), 401 vs 403 reveals whether an admin key is configured, the audit actor of complimentary issuance is a fixed string.
acceptance: Rate limit returns 429 when exceeded (tested)
Max quantity per order enforced
No secrets in repository (secret scanning step in CI)
docs/security.md documents threats and mitigations (retries, idempotency, resource abuse)

name: spec-traceability-and-decisions-register
title: Spec traceability and register of own decisions
description: Make explicit, and keep up to date, what the statement asks for and what we decided ourselves. docs/requirements.md is a traceability matrix derived from the original statement (PDF); docs/decisions.md is the register of decisions NOT required by the statement (interpretation of the statement or own extra), each with a DP-NNN id. The harness keeps both alive: feature_list.json carries an origin (spec/interpretation/own) and the decisions ids on every feature, init.sh validates them mechanically, CHECKPOINTS.md (C13), AGENTS.md and the pull request template make the register part of every feature. Documentation and harness only: no application code changes.
acceptance: docs/requirements.md: traceability matrix derived from the ORIGINAL PDF text (re-extracted, not from memory): every functional requirement, technical requirement, deliverable, security and cloud-native item -> status (met / met with interpretation / partial / design only / not met) -> where it is implemented (files/classes) -> evidence (tests, ITs, docs); honest about gaps and interpretations

docs/decisions.md: register of decisions NOT required by the statement, classified as interpretation of the statement or own extra, each with id (DP-NNN), feature, what, why, how to configure/change/remove, impact/risk and status; seeded with the real existing ones (max 10 tickets per order, Idempotency-Key rules, rate limiting and admin lockout, complimentary endpoint + admin key, input limits, management port, security headers, hardening, etc.), each verified against the code

feature_list.json gets an origin field (spec/interpretation/own) on every feature and decisions ids for non-spec ones; init.sh validates it mechanically (valid origin, referenced DP ids exist, no orphan DP, no duplicate or malformed ids, valid matrix statuses), with negative controls proving the validator fails when it should
CHECKPOINTS.md (new checkpoint C13), AGENTS.md (workflow) and .github/pull_request_template.md make the register part of every feature/PR
README links both documents; every path/link in the new docs resolves; no application code changed

name: stabilize-integration-tests
title: Stabilize the integration tests (CI timeouts)
description: Outcome of the investigation of the CI failure of run 37128517785 (HardeningEndToEndIT.securityHeaders_...): the initial hypothesis (default 5 s WebTestClient timeout) was REFUTED by the CI report artifact: the class already had a 30 s timeout, the failing call was the last trivial request (GET /actuator/health -> 404) and it received no response at all in 30 s (the test normally takes 0.27 s). The real hang was NOT reproduced and its cause is UNKNOWN (tracked in F-033 / issue #63). What this feature does deliver (test-only): one shared timeout policy for every WebTestClient (property spring.test.webtestclient.timeout=60s for injected clients, TestWebClients for hand-built ones, shared constants in TestTimeouts), an audit of the other fixed waits, a guard test that fails when a test breaks the policy, and a defensive fix (read the response body so pooled connections are returned). It removes a source of false failures; it does NOT prevent the observed hang.
acceptance: Root cause of the 5 s hypothesis checked against the CI artifact and refuted; the observed failure documented as an unexplained 30 s no-response hang
Every WebTestClient used by the tests goes through one shared timeout mechanism; other fixed waits audited; no assertion weakened; guard test in place
No production code change

Stability evidence by execution: full integration suite green several times in a row and once under CPU load; the 5 s failure mode reproduced deterministically with a negative control (the original 30 s hang was not reproduced)
Registered as DP-035 in docs/decisions.md and linked from feature_list.json (origin own); the unexplained hang is followed up in F-033

name: pin-ci-runner-image
title: Pin the CI runner image (ubuntu-24.04)
description: GitHub announced that the ubuntu-latest label migrates to Ubuntu 26 on 2026-10-19 (https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748). ci.yml, security.yml and release.yml use ubuntu-latest, so the OS would change under us without any commit. Pin every runs-on to the explicit image that ubuntu-latest resolves to today, document how to move deliberately, and add an init.sh guard that rejects floating runner labels.

Workflows validated (actionlint via Docker) and the verify + Security checks green on the PR
Documented how and when to move to the next image deliberately (a dated note in docs/verification.md or the README CI/CD section; Dependabot does not bump runner labels)
Registered as a decision in docs/decisions.md (DP-036) and linked from feature_list.json (origin own)
init.sh fails when a workflow uses a floating runner label (-latest), proven with negative controls

name: enforce-reservation-ttl-cap
title: Enforce the 10-minute maximum of the reservation TTL
description: The statement says tickets are reserved temporarily "máximo 10 minutos". ticketflow.reservation.ttl defaults to PT10M but is only validated as positive: nothing prevents configuring PT2H, which would contradict the requirement. Define the cap as a named constant and reject a larger TTL at startup with a clear message.
acceptance: A reservation TTL above 10 minutes is rejected at startup with a clear message (fail fast); values from 1 s up to PT10M stay valid and the default is unchanged. The cap is a named constant tied to the requirement (no magic number), enforced where the TTL is validated, and covered by unit tests (boundary: exactly PT10M ok, PT10M + 1 ns rejected, zero/negative rejected) and by an application-context test proving the app refuses to start with an over-limit value.
End-to-end proof against the real stack: the TTL used by POST /orders never exceeds 10 minutes.
docs/requirements.md (RF-2) and the existing decision about the configurable TTL in docs/decisions.md updated; README configuration table says the maximum.
No behaviour change for the default configuration.

name: enable-runtime-components-by-default
title: Run the full pipeline by default (consumer and expiry job enabled)
description: ticketflow.sqs.consumer.enabled and ticketflow.expiration.enabled default to false; only docker-compose turns them on. Anyone starting the app another way gets a system that accepts purchases but never processes them (orders stay RESERVED) and never releases expired reservations, which breaks the statement's asynchronous-processing and automatic-release requirements by default. Both flags now default to true; the API-only role stays possible with explicit false.
acceptance: Both flags default to true (single source of truth: @ConfigurationProperties defaults + application.yml + README table, and the @ConditionalOnProperty guards use matchIfMissing). The API-only role stays possible with explicit false (documented for the api/worker split in docs/aws.md); proven by tests that start a context WITHOUT the property (components present) and with =false (absent).

The existing test contexts keep passing WITHOUT weakening any assertion: ONE shared test-resources mechanism (src/test/resources/application.properties, not an application.yml that would shadow the main one) sets false for the suite; tests that need the components set true explicitly.
Startup with the components enabled but SQS/DynamoDB unreachable still behaves gracefully (retry with backoff, readiness DOWN, no crash loop): proven by a test.

End-to-end proof: run the packaged app WITHOUT any enabling variable and show purchase -> SOLD and a reservation expiring; API-only role with explicit false leaves the order RESERVED; app with unreachable infrastructure stays up with readiness DOWN.

docs/requirements.md, docs/decisions.md (new DP-037 + DP-006 and DP-012 updated), README, docs/aws.md, docs/observability.md, docs/architecture.md and docker-compose comments updated; full INCLUDE_INTEGRATION=true ./init.sh green and stable (at least 3 times in a row).

name: fix-startup-race-missing-tables
title: Requests accepted before the DynamoDB tables exist return 500 instead of 503 (startup race)
description: Tables are provisioned (ApplicationReady) after the web server already accepts traffic (pre-existing since F-006). A request arriving in that window hits DynamoDB ResourceNotFoundException ('Cannot do operations on a non-existent table'), which is not classified and falls into the generic 500, while readiness already says DOWN. Reproduced: POST /events polled from the first instant after docker-compose up (no --wait) returned 500 internal-error, then 201. A temporary, expected condition must be 503 + Retry-After, not a misleading 500.
acceptance: A deterministic regression test (full context, real DynamoDB Local, tables NOT provisioned) reproduces the window and fails today with 500 on the API routes that touch DynamoDB; the same routes work normally once the tables exist, and business errors (404/409) are unchanged.

The fix is the smallest correct one, justified against the alternatives (classify ResourceNotFoundException as transient 503 + Retry-After; provision before the web server accepts traffic; a filter answering 503 until provisioning ends). It must not hide a real misconfiguration forever (readiness stays DOWN, full exception logged server-side), must not hang or crash when DynamoDB is unreachable (F-031), leaks nothing internal, and increments the F-024 dependency-unavailable metric.

Polling experiment against the real stack (docker-compose up WITHOUT --wait, POST /events from the first instant) repeated at least 10 times and once under CPU load: before the fix a 500 appears, after the fix only connection errors, then 503 (with Retry-After), then 201; never a 500.

No existing mapping or test weakened; README error catalogue and startup behaviour, docs/observability.md (if semantics change) and docs/decisions.md (DP-038, Extra propio) updated; ./init.sh and INCLUDE_INTEGRATION=true ./init.sh green.
